claims.source_quote_ar: فهذا تنبيه على أن الأمر كله للَّه
claims.claim_ar: الآية تؤدى كـتنبيه/تحذير إخلاقي؛ الخطاب يؤطر الحكم الأخلاقي بإظهار تبعية الأمر كله للَّه وتحذير من عاقبة الكذب على الله.
claims.claim_en: The verse functions as an admonitory/ didactic style: the discourse frames the moral judgment by asserting that all affairs belong to God and warning about the consequences of fabricating lies against Him.

claims.claim_ar: عبارة (مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ) تعمل تقييدًا زمنيًا: تُقيّد وقوع (افترى الكذب) بأنه بعد حدثٍ سابق، فتمنع التعميم وتحدد الزمان.
claims.claim_en: The phrase (min baʿdi dhālika / 'after that') functions as a temporal restriction: it confines the occurrence of 'fabricating lies' to a time following a prior event, preventing a blanket generalization and specifying timing.
claims.needs_review_reason: Assigning this phrasing to the technical device 'hasr_qasr' is interpretive (restrictive nuance); corroboration with classical definitions advised.

claims.claim_ar: افتتاح بـ(فمن) ثم الانتقال إلى الحكم القطعي في الجملة اللاحقة يمثل التفاتًا بلاغيًّا: من حالة افتراضية أو شرطية إلى عبارة تقريرية حاسمة (فأولئك هم الظالمون).
claims.claim_en: Beginning with (fa-man) and then moving to the categorical verdict in the subsequent clause constitutes a rhetorical shift (iltifat): from a hypothetical/conditional frame to an emphatic, definitive judgment (fa-ulā'ika hum al-ẓālimūn).
claims.needs_review_reason: Labeling this specific transition as 'iltifat' is interpretive; some scholars may classify it differently (e.g., simple conditional → apodosis).

warnings: Source quotes are taken from the provided commentary chunks (Zamakhsharī) and are used as attestations of rhetorical observations; they may not be direct exegesis of Sūrah 3:94 itself. Verify with the particular classical authors requested (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, tafsīr-balāgha) if strict provenance to those authors is required.

Some device assignments (especially distinguishing 'iltifat' vs. ordinary conditional/apodosis, and tagging 'مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ' as 'hasr_qasr') are interpretive; confidence levels note where further specialist review is recommended.
